title: Biochemistry
description: Biochemistry explains life through molecular structure, chemical reactivity, energy transformation, information flow, and regulated networks. Students learn to reason from water and weak interactions to protein folding, enzyme mechanism, membranes, metabolism, signaling, and gene expression. They interpret quantitative biochemical evidence and apply these ideas to biological discovery, chemical mechanism, nutrition, and disease. All three degree groups complete the same conceptual and quantitative core, with discipline-specific cases and capstone choices rather than separate syllabi.

resources.title: Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry
resources.description: Nelson and Cox. Comprehensive shared reference for structure, enzymology, metabolism, bioenergetics, regulation, and molecular biology.

resources.title: Biochemistry (Berg, Tymoczko, Gatto, and Stryer)
resources.description: Strong conceptual narrative, molecular mechanism, protein function, and pathway logic. Used by MIT 7.05.

resources.title: Biochemistry (Miesfeld and McEvoy)
resources.description: Readable mechanistic treatment and contemporary examples. An MIT-listed alternative.

resources.title: Biochemistry (Voet and Voet)
resources.description: Deeper chemistry, physical basis, enzymology, and metabolic detail for Chemistry students and instructor enrichment.

resources.title: Biochemistry Free For All
resources.description: Oregon State University. Free course-length reference, figures, and review support.

resources.title: MIT OCW 7.05 General Biochemistry
resources.description: Undergraduate lectures, problem sets, exams, and a metabolism-centered second half.

resources.title: MIT OCW 5.07SC Biological Chemistry I
resources.description: Chemistry-forward explanations of recurring reaction types, bioenergetics, and pathway mechanisms.

resources.title: ASBMB core concepts and exam goals
resources.description: Outcome map for energy/metabolism, structure/function, information transfer, scientific skills, homeostasis, and evolution.

resources.title: RCSB Protein Data Bank and PDB-101
resources.description: Macromolecular structures, molecular visualization, structure-function cases, and accessible teaching materials. Also https://pdb101.rcsb.org/.

resources.title: UniProt
resources.description: Curated sequence, function, localization, variants, cofactors, and cross-references.

resources.title: BRENDA
resources.description: Enzyme reactions, kinetic parameters, organisms, substrates, inhibitors, and literature links.

resources.title: KEGG and Reactome
resources.description: Pathway context, molecular participants, disease links, and comparative network exploration. Also https://reactome.org/.

resources.title: PubChem
resources.description: Structures, properties, identifiers, bioassays, and safety/context for metabolites, cofactors, and inhibitors.

resources.title: NCBI Bookshelf
resources.description: Free authoritative books and chapters for molecular biology, metabolism, nutrition, genetics, and disease.

resources.title: iBiology and HHMI BioInteractive
resources.description: Research-facing lectures, animations, case materials, and connections between biochemical concepts and discovery. Also https://www.biointeractive.org/.

resources.title: Python: Jupyter, NumPy, SciPy, pandas, Matplotlib
resources.description: Reproducible curve fitting, pathway accounting, data visualization, uncertainty analysis, and report-ready notebooks. Also https://scipy.org/.

topics.title: Water, pH, Buffers, and Biochemical Thermodynamics
topics.description: This opening unit gives students the chemical environment of life. It explains why water, weak acids, noncovalent interactions, and energy changes determine what biomolecules can do.

children.title: Water and noncovalent interactions
children.description: Students learn why water shapes biomolecular structure and reactivity. The gist is that hydrogen bonding, polarity, and hydrophobic effects organize biological systems.

children.title: pH and buffers
children.description: Students learn how cells control proton concentration. This matters because charge, structure, and enzyme activity depend on pH.

children.title: Thermodynamics in biology
children.description: Students learn how free energy predicts whether biochemical processes are favorable.

children.title: Redox logic
children.description: Students learn how electron transfer powers metabolism.

topics.title: Amino Acids, Peptides, and Protein Structure
topics.description: This unit introduces proteins as polymers with chemically diverse building blocks. Students learn how sequence and folding create molecular function.

children.title: Amino acid chemistry
children.description: Students learn the structures and properties that determine protein behavior.

children.title: Peptides and primary structure
children.description: Students learn how amino acids are linked and read as sequences.

children.title: Higher-order structure
children.description: Students learn how local and global folding create stable shapes.

children.title: Protein folding and stability
children.description: Students learn why proteins fold and what can disrupt them.

topics.title: Protein Function, Hemoglobin, and Structure-Function Relationships
topics.description: This unit connects protein shape to biological work. Students learn how binding, conformational change, and cooperativity turn structure into function.

children.title: Ligand binding
children.description: Students learn how proteins recognize and bind molecules.

children.title: Hemoglobin and myoglobin
children.description: Students study classic oxygen-binding proteins to see structure-function logic in action.

children.title: Allostery
children.description: Students learn how one site on a protein can regulate another.

children.title: Protein dysfunction
children.description: Students connect molecular changes to physiology and disease.

topics.title: Enzyme Kinetics, Mechanisms, and Regulation
topics.description: Enzymes are biological catalysts. This unit teaches students how enzymes accelerate reactions, how rates are measured, and how activity is controlled.

children.title: Catalytic strategies
children.description: Students learn how enzymes lower activation energy.

children.title: Michaelis-Menten kinetics
children.description: Students learn the basic model for enzyme rate behavior.

children.title: Inhibition
children.description: Students learn how inhibitors change enzyme behavior and why this matters for drugs and regulation.

children.title: Regulation of enzyme activity
children.description: Students learn how cells tune pathway flux.

topics.title: Carbohydrates, Glycobiology, and Glycolysis/Gluconeogenesis
topics.description: This unit moves from carbohydrate structure to central glucose metabolism. Students learn how sugars serve as fuels, structural molecules, and information-bearing cell-surface components.

children.title: Carbohydrate structure
children.description: Students learn the chemical forms and linkages of sugars.

children.title: Glycobiology
children.description: Students learn that carbohydrates are also signals and structural decorations.

children.title: Glycolysis
children.description: Students learn how glucose is converted to pyruvate while capturing ATP and reducing power.

children.title: Gluconeogenesis and glycogen
children.description: Students learn how organisms maintain glucose availability.

children.title: Pentose phosphate pathway and redox balance
children.description: Students learn how glucose carbon supplies NADPH and ribose while supporting antioxidant defense and biosynthesis.

topics.title: Citric Acid Cycle, Electron Transport, and Oxidative Phosphorylation
topics.description: This unit explains how cells extract large amounts of energy from fuel. Students learn how carbon oxidation, electron transport, and proton gradients are coupled to ATP synthesis.

children.title: Pyruvate oxidation and TCA cycle
children.description: Students learn how acetyl-CoA enters a cyclic pathway that harvests reducing equivalents.

children.title: Electron transport chain
children.description: Students learn how electrons move through membrane complexes.

children.title: Chemiosmosis
children.description: Students learn how electron transfer creates a proton gradient.

children.title: Regulation and inhibitors
children.description: Students learn how energy production responds to cellular demand and toxins.

topics.title: Lipids, Membranes, and Membrane Transport
topics.description: This unit covers hydrophobic biomolecules and the membranes they form. Students learn how membrane structure enables compartmentalization, signaling, and transport.

children.title: Lipid classes
children.description: Students learn the main biological lipid families and what their structures imply.

children.title: Membrane structure
children.description: Students learn why membranes are dynamic selective barriers.

children.title: Membrane transport
children.description: Students learn how molecules cross membranes.

children.title: Membrane potential and gradients
children.description: Students learn how gradients store usable energy.

topics.title: Lipid Metabolism and Membrane Signaling
topics.description: This unit explains lipid synthesis and breakdown as energy storage and signaling. Students learn why lipid metabolism is central to fasting, feeding, hormones, and disease.

children.title: Fatty acid oxidation
children.description: Students learn how fatty acids are mobilized and broken down for energy.

children.title: Fatty acid synthesis
children.description: Students learn how excess energy can be stored as lipid.

children.title: Cholesterol and lipoproteins
children.description: Students learn the biochemical basis of sterol metabolism and transport.

children.title: Lipid signaling
children.description: Students learn how lipids act as signals, not just fuel.

topics.title: Amino Acid, Nitrogen, and Urea Cycle Metabolism
topics.description: This unit explains how organisms handle amino groups and carbon skeletons. Students learn why nitrogen metabolism requires careful detoxification.

children.title: Amino acid catabolism
children.description: Students learn how amino acids are broken down and routed into central metabolism.

children.title: Nitrogen disposal
children.description: Students learn why ammonia is toxic and how the body converts it into safer forms.

children.title: Amino acid biosynthesis
children.description: Students learn the broad logic of making nonessential amino acids.

children.title: Clinical and nutrition links
children.description: Students connect nitrogen metabolism to diet and disease.

topics.title: Nucleotides, Nucleic Acids, and Nucleotide Metabolism
topics.description: This unit connects biochemical building blocks to genetic information and energy transfer. Students learn how nucleotides are made, used, salvaged, and degraded.

children.title: Nucleotide structure
children.description: Students learn the chemical parts of nucleotides and nucleic acids.

children.title: DNA and RNA chemistry
children.description: Students learn how nucleic acid structure supports information storage and expression.

children.title: Nucleotide biosynthesis and salvage
children.description: Students learn how cells balance costly de novo synthesis with recycling.

children.title: Nucleotide degradation and disease
children.description: Students learn how breakdown pathways can produce clinically important metabolites.

topics.title: Metabolic Integration and Hormonal Regulation
topics.description: This unit asks how pathways work together across tissues and nutritional states. Students learn metabolism as an integrated system rather than isolated charts.

children.title: Fed and fasting states
children.description: Students learn how metabolism changes after meals and during fasting.

children.title: Hormonal regulation
children.description: Students learn how endocrine signals coordinate pathway flux.

children.title: Tissue specialization
children.description: Students learn why liver, muscle, adipose tissue, brain, and red blood cells use fuels differently.

children.title: Metabolic disease
children.description: Students connect regulation to pathology and nutrition.

children.title: Receptor and nutrient-sensing pathways
children.description: Students connect extracellular signals and nutrient status to enzyme phosphorylation, gene expression, growth, and pathway flux.

topics.title: Molecular Biology Connections: DNA, RNA, Proteins, and Gene Regulation
topics.description: Biochemistry overlaps with molecular biology because molecules carry and execute genetic instructions. Students learn how nucleic acids and proteins connect metabolism to gene expression.

children.title: DNA replication and repair
children.description: Students learn the biochemical logic of copying and maintaining DNA.

children.title: Transcription and RNA processing
children.description: Students learn how RNA is produced and matured.

children.title: Translation
children.description: Students learn how genetic information becomes protein sequence.

children.title: Gene regulation
children.description: Students learn how cells control protein production.

topics.title: Biochemical Methods, Databases, and Pathway Analysis
topics.description: This unit teaches students how biochemical knowledge is generated and used. It connects wet-lab techniques, structural data, sequence databases, and pathway maps.

children.title: Protein purification and analysis
children.description: Students learn how proteins are separated and characterized.

children.title: Enzyme and metabolite assays
children.description: Students learn how pathway activity can be measured.

children.title: Structural and sequence databases
children.description: Students learn to use public resources as scientific tools.

children.title: Pathway analysis
children.description: Students learn how to read and interpret metabolic maps.

children.title: Experimental design, quantitation, and reproducibility
children.description: Students learn how controls, calibration, replication, uncertainty, and transparent workflows turn measurements into defensible biochemical evidence.

topics.title: Clinical, Nutrition, and Disease Applications of Biochemistry
topics.description: The final unit applies biochemical principles to health, nutrition, pharmacology, and disease. Students learn why molecular mechanisms matter outside the classroom.

children.title: Nutrition and metabolism
children.description: Students connect nutrients to biochemical pathways.

children.title: Clinical biochemistry
children.description: Students learn how biochemical measurements support diagnosis and monitoring.

children.title: Drug and toxicology connections
children.description: Students learn why enzymes and pathways matter for drug action and toxicity.

children.title: Inherited and acquired disorders
children.description: Students integrate pathway logic with disease examples.

children.title: Oxidative stress and cancer metabolism
children.description: Students examine how redox imbalance and metabolic rewiring alter cell survival, biosynthesis, and interpretation of disease biomarkers.

children.title: Reactive oxygen species and antioxidant systems
